{{CS1 config|mode=cs2}}
The '''Orlicz–Pettis theorem''' is a theorem in [[functional analysis]] concerning [[convergent series]] (Orlicz) or, equivalently, [[countable additivity]] of [[measure (mathematics)|measures]] (Pettis) with values in abstract spaces.

Let <math>X </math> be a Hausdorff [[locally convex topological vector space]] with dual <math> X^*</math>.  A series <math>\sum_{n=1}^\infty~x_n </math>  is  ''subseries convergent'' (in <math> X </math>), if all its subseries <math>\sum_{k=1}^\infty~ x_{n_k}</math> are convergent. The theorem says that, equivalently,
 
*(i) If a series <math> \sum_{n=1}^\infty~x_n </math>  is weakly subseries convergent in <math>X </math>  (i.e., is subseries convergent in  <math>X </math>  with respect to its weak topology <math>\sigma(X,X^*)</math>), then it is (subseries) convergent; or 
*(ii) Let <math> \mathbf{A} </math>  be a <math>\sigma</math>-algebra of sets and let <math>\mu:\mathbf{A}\to X </math> be an [[additive set function]]. If <math>\mu </math> is weakly countably additive, then it is countably additive (in the original topology of the space <math>X </math>).

The history of the origins of the theorem is somewhat complicated. In numerous papers and books there are misquotations or/and misconceptions concerning the result.  Assuming that  <math>X </math>  is weakly sequentially complete Banach space, [[Władysław Orlicz|W. Orlicz]]<ref>W. Orlicz, [http://matwbn.icm.edu.pl/ksiazki/sm/sm1/sm1114.pdf Beiträge zur Theorie der Orthogonalentwicklungen II], ''[[Studia Mathematica]]'' '''1''' (1929),  241–255.</ref> proved the following

'''Theorem.'''  If a series  <math> \sum_{n=1}^\infty~x_n </math> is weakly unconditionally Cauchy, i.e., <math> \sum_{n=1}^\infty |x^*(x_n)|<\infty </math>  for each linear functional  <math>x^*\in X^* </math>, then the series is (norm) convergent in  <math> X </math>.

After the paper was published, Orlicz realized that in the proof of the theorem the weak sequential completeness of  <math>X </math>  was only used to guarantee the existence of the weak limits of the considered series. Consequently, assuming the existence of those limits, which amounts to the assumption of the weak subseries convergence of the series, the same proof shows that the series in norm convergent. In other words, the version (i) of the Orlicz–Pettis theorem holds. 
The theorem in this form, openly credited to Orlicz, appeared in Banach's monograph<ref>Théorie des opérations linéaires, Monografje matematyczne, Warszawa 1932; Oeuvres. Vol. II}, PWN, Warszawa 1979.</ref> in the last chapter ''Remarques'' in which no proofs were provided. [[Billy James Pettis|Pettis]] directly referred to Orlicz's theorem in Banach's book. Needing the result in order to show the coincidence of the weak and strong measures, he provided a proof.<ref>B.J. Pettis, [https://www.ams.org/journals/tran/1938-044-02/S0002-9947-1938-1501970-8/S0002-9947-1938-1501970-8.pdf On integration in vector spaces],''Trans. Amer. Math. Soc.'' '''44''' (1938), 277–304.</ref> Also [[Nelson Dunford|Dunford]] gave a proof<ref>N. Dunford, [https://www.ams.org/journals/tran/1938-044-02/S0002-9947-1938-1501971-X/S0002-9947-1938-1501971-X.pdf Uniformity in linear spaces], ''Trans. Amer. Math. Soc.'' '''44''' (1938), 305–356.</ref>  (with a remark that it is similar to the original proof of Orlicz).

A more thorough discussion of the origins of the Orlicz–Pettis theorem and, in particular, of the paper<ref>W. Orlicz, [http://matwbn.icm.edu.pl/ksiazki/sm/sm1/sm1114.pdf Beiträge zur Theorie der Orthogonalentwicklungen II], ''[[Studia Mathematica]]'' '''1''' (1929),  241–255.</ref> can be found in.<ref>W. Filter and I. Labuda,  [https://math.wp.olemiss.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/96/2018/07/filter-labuda.pdf Essays on the Orlicz-Petts theorem, I (The two theorems)], ''[[Real Analysis Exchange]]'' '''16(2)''', 1990-91, 393--403.</ref> See also footnote 5 on p.&nbsp;839 of<ref>W. Orlicz, Collected works, Vol.1, PWN-Polish Scientific Publishers, Warszawa 1988.</ref>  and the comments at the end of Section 2.4 of the 2nd edition of the quoted book by Albiac and Kalton. Though in Polish, there is also an adequate comment on page 284 of the quoted monograph of [[Andrzej Alexiewicz|Alexiewicz]],  Orlicz's first PhD-student,<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=51907&fChrono=1|title = Władysław Orlicz - the Mathematics Genealogy Project}}</ref> still in the occupied Lwów.

== Orlicz-Pettis type theorems ==
The theorem of Orlicz and Pettis had been strengthened and generalized in many directions. An early survey of this area of research is Kalton's paper.<ref>Nigel Kalton, [http://kaltonmemorial.missouri.edu/docs/Cont.Math1980.pdf The Orlicz-Pettis theorem] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170918155108/http://kaltonmemorial.missouri.edu/docs/Cont.Math1980.pdf |date=2017-09-18 }}, ''Contemporary Mathematics'' '''2''' (1980), 91–100.</ref> A natural setting for subseries convergence is that of an [[Abelian group|Abelian]] [[topological group]] <math> X </math> and a representative result of this area of research is the following theorem, called by Kalton the Graves-Labuda-Pachl Theorem.<ref>Iwo Labuda, [https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/1385725879900064 Universal measurability and summable families in topological vector spaces], ''Indagationes Mathematicae (N. S.)'' '''82'''(1979), 27-34.</ref><ref>J. K. Pachl, [https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/1385725879900076 A note on the Orlicz-Pettis Theorem], ''Indagationes Mathematicae (N. S.)'''82''''' (1979), 35-37.</ref><ref>W. H. Graves, [https://www.ams.org/journals/proc/1979-073-01/S0002-9939-1979-0512056-5/S0002-9939-1979-0512056-5.pdf Universal Lusin measurability and subfamily summable families in Abelian topological groups], ''[[Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society]]'' '''73'''  (1979), 45--50.</ref>

'''Theorem.''' Let <math> X </math> be an Abelian group and <math> \alpha ,\beta </math> two Hausdorff group topologies on <math> X </math> such that <math>(X,\beta)</math> is sequentially complete, <math> \alpha \subset \beta </math>, and the identity <math> j:(X,\alpha)\to (X,\beta)</math> is universally measurable. Then the subseries convergence for both topologies  <math>\alpha </math> and <math>\beta </math> is the same.

As a consequence, if <math>(X,\beta)</math> is a sequentially complete [[K-analytic space|K-analytic]] group, then the conclusion of the theorem is true for ''every'' Hausdorff group topology <math>\alpha</math> weaker than <math>\beta</math>. This is a generalization of an analogical result for a sequentially complete [[analytic space|analytic]] group  <math> (X,\beta)</math><ref>N. J. M. Andersen and J. P. R. Christensen, [https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/BF02757080.pdf Some results on Borel structures with applications to subseries convergence in Abelian topological groups], ''[[Israel Journal of Mathematics]]'' '''15''' (1973), 414--420.</ref> (in the original statement of the Andersen-Christensen theorem the assumption of sequential completeness is missing<ref>I. Labuda, [https://www.researchgate.net/publication/320835884_Measure_Category_and_Convergent_Series], ''[[Real Analysis Exchange|Real Anal. Exchange]]''  '''32(2)''' (2017), 411--428.</ref>), which in turn extends the corresponding theorem of Kalton for a [[Polish space|Polish]] group,<ref>[[Nigel Kalton|N. J. Kalton]], [https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/BF02771728.pdf Subseries convergence in topological groups and vector measures], ''[[Israel Journal of Mathematics]]'' '''10''' (1971), 402-412.</ref> a theorem that triggered this series of papers.

The limitations for this kind of results are provided by the weak* topology of the Banach space  <math>\ell^\infty </math>  and the examples of F-spaces <math> X </math>  with separating dual <math> X^*</math> such that the weak (i.e.,  <math>\sigma(X,X^*) </math>)  subseries convergence does not imply the subseries convergence in the F-norm of the space <math> X </math>.<ref>M. Nawrocki, [https://www.ams.org/journals/proc/1987-101-03/S0002-9939-1987-0908655-3/S0002-9939-1987-0908655-3.pdf On the Orlicz-Pettis property in non-locally convex F-spaces], ''[[Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society]]'' '''101'''(1987), 492--–496.</ref><ref>M. Nawrocki, [https://www.ams.org/journals/proc/1990-109-04/S0002-9939-1990-1007507-0/S0002-9939-1990-1007507-0.pdf The Orlicz-Pettis theorem fails for Lumer's Hardy spaces <math> (LH)^p(B) </math>], ''[[Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society]]'' '''109''' (1990), 957–963.</ref>
